An Operating System is the most important program running on a computer system. It manages all hardware and software resources, provides an interface to interact with the system and facilitates the execution of user applications.

The course focuses on principles of operation, algorithms and data structures essential in Operating Systems functionality. Students passing this course will have an understanding of Operating Systems functionality and internal components; they will be able to write code relevant for OS operation and development. The course uses Linux as a primary case study.

Design principles in operating systems. System calls. Shell scripting. CPU scheduling and processes. I/O and interrupts. Memory management and virtual memory. File system interface and implementation. Protection and security. Virtualization and hypervisors. Examples of different kinds of operating systems. Focus on Linux as a case study.
